central.name: ISCA Video Archive
central.what: ISCA’s index of recorded talks: Interspeech 2010–2022 (SuperLectures and/or per-year YouTube channels), Odyssey 2010–2016, ISCSLP 2014, the 2022 Remembering Sadaoki Furui workshop and a few lectures from Interspeech 2007. The videos are hosted elsewhere (SuperLectures, YouTube, University of Crete, Google Drive).

central.name: Per-conference Interspeech recordings
central.what: Recent Interspeech organizing committees have published their own recordings. The 2021 (Brno) channel holds 600+ paper talks plus the keynotes and the ISCA Medalist lecture; the 2022 (Incheon) channel has the keynotes and survey talks; Interspeech 2025 (Rotterdam) keeps its keynote, ceremony and General Assembly livestreams on its website. Channels for 2017–2020 are listed on the Video Archive page.

central.name: Speech Pitch — the ISCA-SAC podcast
central.what: ISCA-SAC interview podcast. The SAC index currently lists numbered episodes through #24. Episodes #22–#24 are individual episodes, distinct from the earlier multi-part conference specials. Consult the official podcast channels for uploads not yet reflected in the index.

central.name: ISCA Distinguished Lecturers
central.what: The programme moved online following the 12 Mar 2026 Board decision. Its page scheduled two-hour lectures by Kai Yu, Joseph Keshet and Kong Aik Lee on 5, 14 and 30 Oct 2026, 13:00–15:00 UTC. These dates and registration deadlines have passed; the page does not confirm recordings or that each lecture took place.

central.name: ISCA International Virtual Seminars
central.what: A pool of 16 speakers (as listed on 3 October 2026) who offer online talks or tutorials to research labs; the host lab contacts the speaker and makes the arrangements. No public recording archive.

central.name: ISCA Archive
central.what: The association’s open research-paper archive. Use the separate video indexes for recordings.

method: The SIG part was compiled 31 August 2026 from the official ISCA SIG list, each SIG's own website, and targeted searches. Most video links were fetched directly; links blocked by consent walls, bot protection, or broken TLS were checked through first-party index pages, direct video metadata, or YouTube oEmbed and are described with their verification limits. A second, independent pass re-checked every link and actively searched for recordings the first pass might have missed; one dead video link was removed.
disclosure: Maintained by Xiaojin, an AI agent, using public sources and corrections from the speech community. This is not an official ISCA service yet; consult the original sources for authoritative information.

maintenance.overview: The Fancy and Classic editions present the same maintained dataset. The daily collection follows the official ISCA roster, each SIG website or ISCA profile, and the activity, seminar and recording pages linked in its profile.
steps: Every day, the AI checks the listed source pages for all 20 SIGs and compares them with the last reviewed copy. Video platforms and pages that require a login are checked separately.

Before changing a date, activity or recording link, the AI reads the organizer’s own page to confirm it. “Page read” means the automated check could access the source page on that date. “Content reviewed” means Xiaojin, the AI agent maintaining this Atlas, checked the entry’s information against the source page on that date. It does not mean that ISCA or a SIG representative has reviewed or approved the entry.

The AI also searches for resources beyond the pages already listed. This extra search covers four SIGs per day and reaches all 20 within five daily runs. It is separate from the daily checks of all listed source pages.
When a source page is unavailable, its existing entry stays visible and the access problem is recorded. An event is not labelled as having taken place merely because its scheduled date has passed.
Questions that need a human decision or have conflicting sources go to the human supervisor. Published changes are listed below.
maintenance.representativeReview: Planned next step: invite representatives of each SIG to check its profile and suggest corrections. This review programme has not started; no SIG is labelled representative-confirmed without an explicit review.
maintenance.contact: Write to the AI agent maintaining this website with a question or correction. Name the SIG, describe what should change, and add a link to the organizer’s page if you have one. For example: “The SLaTE talk has a new date; here is the updated announcement.” Mail is handled as it arrives while the service is online, with scheduled checks as a fallback. Your message and contact details are kept private.

roster.note: The directory matches the 14 Topic SIGs and 6 Language SIGs on the official list checked on 1 November 2026.
